clue.text: Missing ram adversely affected?

indicators.note: adversely here means turned the opposite way, so the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: something missing is gone, so it is NO (as in 'no ram left')
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmer frets that the absence of a ram has hurt the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adversely' turns the whole two-piece phrase round, not just the ram. 'Affected' is the adjective meaning feigned, as in an affected accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is put on is feigned or assumed, the same sense as an affected manner.

clue.text: Ostentatious display that could weaken the spirit

explanation.definitionFit: A showy display makes a splash, and a splash of soda or water dilutes a measure of whisky or other spirits.

clue.text: Profit distributed when nitrogen gets shared out

indicators.note: the word for shared out gets the nitrogen symbol put within it

parts.note: something shared out is divided
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Gains handed round once a chemical element has been split among the partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's profit paid out to shareholders is its payout per share.

clue.text: What the paper thinks a halter or a leash is?

definitions.text: a halter or a leash is?

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's editorial gives its own view, and a halter or leash is literally an item for leading an animal.

clue.text: Imagines what may be seen at 22

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 22 is TATE, the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to see it in the mind's eye, and paintings hang in the Tate gallery (22 across).

clue.text: Rejects tutors who chop and change

indicators.note: to chop and change is to keep switching about, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Teachers who keep changing their minds turn down applications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chop and change' rearranges the nine letters of TUTORS WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject something is to discard it, as when a court dismisses a case.

clue.text: Bargain offers at the hairdresser's?

parts.note: reductions in charges, read as the fees charged for a haircut at a salon

explanation.surface: A salon advertises special deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Discounted rates are reduced charges, and at a barber's the charge is literally for a cut.

clue.text: Flexible twig and why it is brought in

indicators.note: the word it is brought in, placed inside the word why

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a bendy stick and why it has been fetched indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' is the container signal, not a description of the twig. A withy is a willow shoot used in basketwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow shoot pliable enough to weave baskets is a flexible twig.

clue.text: Rapacious beast turning to run

indicators.note: turning signals that the beast's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the wolf is the proverbially greedy predator

explanation.surface: A greedy animal wheels round and bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses WOLF. 'run' is a noun, as a stream runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Water's movement or a steady stream is a run, as in a run of traffic.

clue.text: Kinky nails put into a perch for a Shakespeare heroine

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are put into the word for a perch

parts.note: a perch is an old unit of length, also called a rod or pole

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of nails are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Bent metal fasteners are hammered into a bird's roost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' scrambles the nails to OSALIN, and 'put into' places that inside the perch. Rosalind is the heroine of As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: The disguised lead of As You Like It is one of the Bard's best-known female leads.

clue.text: Fierce creature about to turn in for a wash.

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the big cat goes round the other piece

parts.note: a lion is a fierce creature

indicators.note: turn signals that the little word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A wild animal is about to go and bathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but the words split: 'about' is the container and 'turn' the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal liquid applied to the skin is a wash, such as an eye wash.

clue.text: Love-torn female destined to go on foot?

indicators.note: torn means split open, so the female pronoun is opened up to take the zero

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lovelorn woman is doomed to walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' splits SHE so that O (love, zero in tennis) goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is made to be worn on the feet, so it is fated to go on one.

clue.text: Fresh tribulation for a district in South London

parts.note: fresh means new
a cross to bear is a trial or tribulation

explanation.surface: A new trouble arises for a neighbourhood south of the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: New Cross is a district of south-east London, near Deptford.
explanation.definitionFit: This area of Lewisham borough is a London neighbourhood south of the river.

clue.text: Estimated value of possessions that may'be'made to disappear

definitions.text: Estimated value of possessions that may'be'made to disappear

parts.words: Estimated value of possessions that may'be'made to disappear
parts.note: valued for insurance, as goods are before a thief might take them; also sounds like prized possessions

explanation.surface: An insurer values property that might be stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: The cryptic hint is the phrase 'a prized' possession, the kind a burglar makes vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods assessed by a valuer have had their worth estimated.

clue.text: Gets bigger meals laid out?

explanation.definitionFit: Something that extends grows larger, and a lavish buffet laid out on a table is a feast set out.

clue.text: Former pirate and' dunderhead are, we hear, lost but redeemed

parts.note: former means ex, as in an ex-husband

indicators.note: lost signals the letter heard in are is dropped from the word pirate
we hear means the word are is taken by its sound, the letter R

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like R
the head of the word dunder is its first letter D

explanation.surface: An ex-buccaneer and a fool are said to be lost souls yet saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'are' into the letter R, and 'lost' removes it from PIRATE to leave PIATE. D comes from the head of 'dunder' in 'dunderhead'.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone for a sin is to make amends, and an atoned wrong has been redeemed.

clue.text: An exercise the newspapers generally take up

parts.note: the press is the collective term for newspapers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something the papers usually adopt as a habit.
explanation.walkthrough: A press-up is the US push-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing the body off the floor with the arms is a gym workout move.

clue.text: Cut-throat bunch of hustlers

indicators.note: a bunch is a jumble of things, so the letters of hustlers are gathered in a new order

explanation.surface: A gang of swindlers is described as vicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunch of' rearranges HUSTLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Merciless competition is cut-throat, without pity.

clue.text: See 4
The fellow who nominated Prospero 'in error

indicators.note: in error means wrongly set, so the letters of Prospero are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly put forward Shakespeare's magician for a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges PROSPERO, the magician of The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who puts a candidate's name forward is the nominator.

clue.text: Lost no time introducing physical education into South Dakota?

indicators.note: introducing one thing into another puts it inside, so the school subject goes inside the state

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota

explanation.surface: Gym classes were brought into a US state without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' puts PE inside SD, the US state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry is to waste no time, and hurried is the past tense of moving fast.

clue.text: A gallery that arouses tremendous excitement initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: An art museum that creates a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'that arouses tremendous excitement'. The Tate is the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: London's national museum of modern and British art is an art gallery.

clue.text: Youthful foreign detective cryptically defining the cancan?

explanation.walkthrough: Tintin is the young Belgian reporter in Hergé's comics; 'can' is a tin, so 'cancan' read as two words is TIN TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hergé's boy reporter from Belgium is a young sleuth, and since can means tin, can-can split up is tin-tin.

clue.text: A sharp male having a whip round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the whip goes around the male

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip, the cat
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A clever man organises a collection for colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: A sharp (sharper) is a swindler. 'whip round' looks like a collection, but the words split: 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharper is a card swindler, someone who defrauds.

clue.text: I'm rebuffed with anger that is more apparent than real

definitions.text: that is more apparent than real

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the letters of I'm are read backwards

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe gives the letters I and M
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A person snubbed responds with fury that is all for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' reverses IM to MI.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion in the desert is a thing more apparent than real.

clue.text: Savoy opera composed in a hotel

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of in a hotel are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan work was written in a hotel room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges IN A HOTEL. Iolanthe is a Gilbert and Sullivan opera, first staged at the Savoy Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's fairy operetta was one of the comic operas staged at the Savoy Theatre.

clue.text: Well-balanced first offender splitting fifty-fifty

indicators.note: the offender is splitting the pair of fifties by sitting between them

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give L and L
Eve was the first sinner in Genesis, eating the forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: A steady, even-handed first-time criminal divides the loot equally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting' puts EVE between L and L (Roman fifty twice).
explanation.definitionFit: Something flat and even is evenly balanced.

clue.text: Not romantic, as Ovid's verses are

explanation.definitionFit: Classicism is the opposite of Romanticism in art, and the Latin poet's works belong to classical antiquity.
